questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, how many maxima can be obtained on a screen (including central maxima), if $\text{d} = \dfrac{5 \lambda}{2 }$ (where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light)?
questions.solution:
In YDSE, path difference, $\Delta \text{x} = \text{d sin} \theta$

For maxima, $\Delta \text{x} = \text{n} \lambda$, where $\text{n} = 0 \text{,} \pm 1 \text{,} \pm 2 \text{....}$

$\dfrac{5 \lambda}{2} \text\sin \theta = \text{n} \lambda$ (given that $\text{d} = \dfrac{5 \lambda}{2}$)

$\begin{array}{ll}⇒ sin\theta = \dfrac{2n}{5} ......... ( i )\end{array}$

Since,$- 1 \le sin\theta \le 1$ Form (i)$⇒ - 1 \le 2n / 5 \le 1$

So, $- \dfrac{5}{2} \le \text{n} \le \dfrac{5}{2}$

So, possible values of n are $\text{-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}$. Thus a total of $\text{5}$ maxima will be obtained.

questions.q: In a Young's double slit experiment using monochromatic light of wavelengths $\lambda$, the intensity of light at a point on the screen with a path difference $\lambda$ is $M$ units and the intensity of light at a point where the path difference is $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$ is $nM$ units. What is the value of $n$?
questions.solution:
Resultant intensity ${\text{I}}_{\text{R}} = {\text{I}}_{1} + {\text{I}}_{2} + 2\sqrt{{\text{I}}_{1}{\text{I}}_{2}}cos\theta$
If path difference, $= \lambda$ then phase difference $= 2\pi \ldots . \left[∵ ϕ = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \Deltax\right]$
$∴ {\text{I}}_{\text{R}} = \text{I} + \text{I} + 2\sqrt{\text{I} \times \text{I}}cos2\pi \ldots . . ( ∵ {\text{I}}_{1} = {\text{I}}_{2} = \text{I} )$
$= 4I = M$
If path difference $= \dfrac{\lambda}{3}$
then phase difference $= \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \dfrac{\lambda}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{rad}$
${I}_{R}^{'} = I + I + 2\sqrt{I \times I}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
$= 2\text{I} + 2\text{I}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) = \text{I} = \dfrac{\text{M}}{4} = 0.25\text{M}$

For fist minimum to occur,

Path difference

$⇒ \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D + x\right)}^{2}} - \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D - x\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

questions.q: YDSE is conducted using light of wavelength $6000\overset{∘}{A}$ to observe an interference pattern. When a film of some material $3 . 0 \times {10}^{- 3}cm$ thick was placed over one of the slits, the fringe pattern shifted by a distance equal to $10$ fringe widths. What is the refractive index of the material of the film?
questions.solution:
Fringe width, $\beta = \dfrac{\lambdaD}{d} . . . \left(i\right)$
where, D: distance between screen and slit
d: distance between two slits
when a film of thickness t and refractive index $\mu$ is placed over one of the slit, the fringe pattern is shift by distance S and is given by $S = \dfrac{( \mu - 1 ) tD}{d} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Given: $S = 10\beta . . . \left(iii\right)$
From equations (i), (ii) and (iii), we get

$\dfrac{( \mu - 1 ) + D}{d} = 10\dfrac{\lambdaD}{d}$

$⇒ \mu - 1 = \dfrac{10\lambda}{t} = \dfrac{10 \times 6000 \times {10}^{- 9}cm}{3 \times {10}^{- 3}cm}$

$⇒ \mu - 1 = 0 . 2$

$⇒ \mu = 1 . 2$

questions.q: One slit of a double-slit experiment is covered by a thin glass plate of refractive index $\text{1}\text{.4}$, and the other by a thin glass plate of the refractive index $\text{1}\text{.7}$. The point on the screen where the central maximum fall before the glass plate was inserted, is now occupied by the fifth bright fringe. Assume the plate have the same thickness $t$ and wavelength of light $\text{480 nm}$, then the value of $t$ is
questions.solution:
Due to the induction of the glass plate, the change in path difference is $\left({\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}\right)t$ .

$∵$ Before inserting the glass plate, the path difference for central maxima is zero.

After introducing glass plate, the change in path difference is equal to $5\lambda$ .

$\left({\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}\right)t = 5\lambda$

$t = \dfrac{5\lambda}{{\mu}_{2} - {\mu}_{1}} = \dfrac{5 \times 480 \times {10}^{- 9}}{1.7 - 1.4}$

$= 8$ micrometre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Unpolarized light of intensity $32W{m}^{- 2}$ passes through three polarizers arranged such that the transmission axes of the first and the last polarizer are at right angles. If the intensity of emerging light is $3W{m}^{- 2}$, then what is the angle (in degree) between the transmission axes of the first two polarizers?
questions.solution:
Since unpolarized light is passing through the first polarizer, hence the intensity of light after crossing the first polarizer will be

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{0} = 16W{m}^{- 2}$

Let us assume that the angle between the transmission axis of the first and second polarizer is $\theta$, then from Malus law we can find out the intensity of light after it crosses the second polarizer.

${I}_{2} = {I}_{1}\cos^{2}\theta = 16\cos^{2}\theta$

Similarly, the intensity of light after crossing the third polarizer is

${I}_{3} = {I}_{2}\cos^{2}\left(90 ° - \theta\right) = 16\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta$

$⇒ {I}_{3} = 16\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta = 3$

$⇒ 4\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ \sin^{2}\left(2\theta\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\theta = 30 °$

questions.q: In Young's double-slit experiment, the distance between slits and the screen is $1m$ and monochromatic light of wavelength $600$ nm is being used. When the separation between the slits is varied, the interference pattern disappears for a particular distance ${d}_{0}$ between the slits. questions.solution:
When the angular fringe width in the interference pattern becomes less than the angular resolving power of the person's eye, the fringes will disappear.

The angular fringe width ${θ}_{0} = \dfrac{\beta}{D} = \dfrac{λ}{{d}_{0}}$

${d}_{0} = \dfrac{λ}{{θ}_{0}} = \dfrac{600 \times {10}^{- 9}}{( \dfrac{1}{60} \times \dfrac{\pi}{180} )}$

$2\text{h} + 2x = \left(n + 1-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda\text{....... (ii)}$

$2\text{h} - 2x = \left(n - 1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda\text{.......(iii)}$

Solving Eqs. (i) and (ii) or Eqs. (i) and (iii), we get,

$2\text{x} = \left(\text{n+}\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda - \left(\text{n} - \dfrac{1 ⁡}{2}\right)\lambda$
$= \lambda$
$\text{x} = \dfrac{λ}{2}$
$\text{x} = \dfrac{λ}{2} = \dfrac{600}{2} = \text{300 nm}$

Path difference $\Delta x = \left(n - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)\lambda$

Because the reflected beam suffers a phase difference of $\pi$.

questions.solution:
Since unpolarized light is passing through the first polarizer, hence the intensity of light after crossing the first polarizer will be

${I}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}{I}_{0} = 16W{m}^{- 2}$

Let us assume that the angle between the transmission axis of the first and second polarizer is $\theta$, then from Malus law we can find out the intensity of light after it crosses the second polarizer.

${I}_{2} = {I}_{1}\cos^{2}\theta = 16\cos^{2}\theta$

${I}_{3} = {I}_{2}\cos^{2}\left(90 ° - \theta\right) = 16\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta$

$⇒ {I}_{3} = 16\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta = 3$

$⇒ 4\cos^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$⇒ \sin^{2}\left(2\theta\right) = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\theta = 30 °$

In a special arrangement of Young's double-slit experiment, the distance between the slits $d$ is twice the distance between the screen and the slits $D$, i.e $d = 2D$. For this setup, the value of $D$ such that the first minima on the screen fall at a distance $D$ from the centre $O$ is found to be $\dfrac{\lambda}{N}$.

What is the value of $N$? [Take $\sqrt{5} = 2 . 24$]

From diagram as provided in question, $OP = x$
$CO = D$
${S}_{1}C = {S}_{2}C = D{T}_{1}P = {T}_{1}O - OP = D - x$
${T}_{2}P = {T}_{2}O + OP = D + x$
Now, ${S}_{1}p = \sqrt{{\left({S}_{1}{T}_{1}\right)}^{2} + {\left({T}_{1}P\right)}^{2}} = \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D - x\right)}^{2}}$

For fist minimum to occur,

Path difference

${S}_{2}P - {S}_{1}P = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D + x\right)}^{2}} - \sqrt{{D}^{2} + {\left(D - x\right)}^{2}} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$⇒ D = \dfrac{\lambda}{2\left(2 . 24 - 1\right)} = \dfrac{\lambda}{2 . 48}$

questions.q: An interference is observed due to two coherent sources $A$ and $B$ separated by a distance $4\lambda$ along Y-axis where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of the light source used. A detector $D$ is moved along the positive X-axis. Find the total number of maxima points are observed on the X-axis excluding the points $x = 0$ and $x = \infty$?
questions.solution:
To obtain maxima the path difference

$AD - BD = n\lambda$

$AD - {x}_{n} = n\lambda$

$AD = n\lambda + {x}_{n}$ ...(i)

Form ${∆}_{le}$ ABD,

$A{D}^{2} = A{B}^{2} + B{D}^{2}$

${\left(n\lambda + {x}_{n}\right)}^{2} = 16{\lambda}^{2} + {x}_{n}^{2}$

${n}^{2}{\lambda}^{2} + {x}_{n}^{2} + 2n\lambda{x}_{n} = 16{\lambda}^{2} + {x}_{n}^{2}$

$2n\lambda{x}_{n} = \left(16 - {n}^{2}\right){\lambda}^{2}$

${x}_{n} = \dfrac{\left(16 - {n}^{2}\right)\lambda}{2n}$

For $n = 0 ⇒ {x}_{0} = \infty$

$n = 1 ⇒ {x}_{1} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 1}{2}\right)\lambda = \dfrac{15\lambda}{2} = 7.5\lambda$

$n = 2 ⇒ {x}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 1}{2}\right)\lambda = \dfrac{12\lambda}{4} = 3\lambda$

$n = 3 ⇒ {x}_{3} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 9}{6}\right)\lambda = \dfrac{7\lambda}{6}$

$n = 4 ⇒ {x}_{4} = \left(\dfrac{16 - 16}{2 \times 4}\right)\lambda = 0$

So the total no. of maxima points observed are 3.

Rays optics is good approximation up to a distance equal to Fresnel's distance $\left({I}_{F}\right)$ .

From the formula of Fresnel's distance,

${D}_{f} = \dfrac{a^{2}}{\lambda}$

Here, $a = 4mm = 4 \times 1{0}^{- 3} m$

$= \dfrac{4 \times 4 \times 1{0}^{- 3} \times 1{0}^{- 3}}{4 \times 1{0}^{- 7}} = 40 m$
